pictures.strongest_point: Reads like a drone photo: warm low sun with long soft shadows, a dense mixed forest of conifers and broadleaf trees with natural variety, and varied ground (field strips, worn paths, grass tones).
pictures.most_visible_faults: Haystacks are perfect smooth half-spheres. Roofs are a uniform clean grey with no weathering. The road's twin ruts are too even and tidy. The field patches are flat rectangles of one colour. Some foreground treetops at bottom left go soft and painterly.

pictures.strongest_point: Plausible layout and aerial haze. The houses sit on the ground and cast believable shadows.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Broadleaf trees are round lollipop blobs, and the same tree is cloned again and again. The grass is a bright flat green with an even speckle pattern. A bare brown dirt ring runs around the forest edge like an unfinished terrain. The forest canopy looks like a game asset rather than leaves.

pictures.strongest_point: The buildings have some surface texture (thatch, timber, brick), and the layout is readable.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Faceted low-poly trees and cone pines. Cartoon mountains with flat colour bands. A plain gradient sky. A flat sand-coloured strip of ground behind the trees, with a hard edge. The grass is one even tone. A big smooth haystack blob sits in the foreground. Overall flat, game-like light.

pictures.strongest_point: A convincing forest mass and clearing seen from above, with soft natural light and believable building scale.
pictures.most_visible_faults: A pine tree grows straight through the round hut at the bottom (the two shapes cut into each other). The road is pale and clean like concrete, with crisp machined grooves. The big lawns are empty and uniform. The thin white birches look pasted on. The haystacks are perfect spheres.

pictures.strongest_point: Tall, varied meadow grass on both sides, a natural sky with thin cloud, and a believable dark forest edge.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The water in the ruts is flat blue streaks that look painted on, with no reflection or depth. The road is smooth powdery sand with evenly scattered pebbles. The cottage plaster is spotless and the thatch smooth like felt. The verge edges are cut in clean lines.

pictures.strongest_point: The thatch and brick surfaces have some texture, and the composition reads clearly.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Faceted low-poly trees and cone pines. A flat empty sky. The road is two raised mounds with grey water channels that look like plastic. The verges are flat pale ground with sparse, identical weed sprites. Almost no ground shadow. The ground surface is smeared noise.

pictures.strongest_point: The most photographic of the set: low golden sun, wet ruts with a puddle that truly reflects the sky, grass growing in the road's centre, mixed grasses, and atmospheric depth to the far cottages.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The thatch is too smooth and even, and the white walls are too clean. The fence rails are new and straight. The cone-roofed hut looks like a woven basket. The conifer silhouettes are a little repetitive. There is no clutter or wear around the doors.

pictures.strongest_point: Hazy depth down the road and dappled sunlight on wet ruts. The flowering grass verge is lively.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The big conifer on the right has stripy, comb-like foliage that looks stylised. The bushes are rounded blobs. The cottage looks like a toy: the roof is smooth clay with no straw, the walls are flat cream and the outlines are blocky. A visible repeating cobble pattern sits bottom left. The colours lean game-like.

pictures.strongest_point: Decent building construction, with a shingle roof, plank walls, a cart and barrels, under soft daylight.
pictures.most_visible_faults: All the wood is one clean, even grey-brown with no wear or grime. The foreground grass is identical tufts stuck on a flat green base. The tree at top left has stylised comb foliage. The cart sits at an awkward angle. The dirt yard is smooth and featureless. Overall it reads like a game asset.

pictures.strongest_point: Weathered silver-grey timber, moss on the shingles, a strong wall of real-looking spruces, warm low sun and natural foreground grass make a convincing rural scene.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The puddles are flat black patches that read as holes, not water. The trough, rail and posts look brand new with sharp edges. The planks are too uniform. The mud has a soft, sculpted, even look. There is little dirt splash on the base of the walls.

pictures.strongest_point: Good stable construction and a believable spruce backdrop. The roof moss gives some age.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Evenly sprinkled green-grey pebble dots cover the yard like a pattern. A pitch-black hole-shaped puddle sits in the foreground. A strange dark round blotch lies under the hitching rail. The light is flat midday. The moss patches repeat in a grid. The haystack is a perfect dome. The ground looks like smooth plaster.

pictures.strongest_point: The shingle roof has a weathered texture with moss variation.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Faceted low-poly trees. An umbrella-shaped toy tree at top left. A flat green and sand background band with a hard horizon. The foreground ground is a heavily smeared, repeating mulch texture. The stone base is cartoonish. The light is flat with no real shadows.

pictures.strongest_point: The stone well has a reasonably detailed rock texture.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Huge faceted low-poly trees. The wall panels have swirly cartoon plaster lines. The ground is a flat green plane with sparse identical weeds and a hard far edge. The sky is plain. The rope and bracket on the well look stylised. Everything is flat-lit and clean.

pictures.strongest_point: Strong timber-frame cottage with stone footing, rich tall grass and a natural sky and treeline.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The thatch has a streaky, motion-blurred look, and stray straws hang in mid-air in front of the walls like floating hairs. The thick eave reads as a soft cushion. The timber frame is ruler-straight and clean. The barrel and bench look new.

pictures.strongest_point: Soft hazy light with a pleasing depth falloff to the back, and plausible props (log pile, stump, bench).
pictures.most_visible_faults: The thatch looks like brushed fabric or a rug, not straw bundles. Flowers are sprinkled evenly like confetti. The fence and stone steps are crisp and new. The leaves at right are flat cut-out shapes. The walls and timber are very clean. The windows are dark voids.

pictures.strongest_point: Very convincing meadow grass, natural sky with cloud, good tree and spruce backdrop, and a distant cottage and well that sit naturally in the haze.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The roof reads as scaly shingles or clay, not thatch, and has a smooth padded eave band. The timber lines are perfectly straight. The plaster is only lightly stained. The bench and pot are tidy and placed. The trodden patch at the door is faint.

pictures.strongest_point: Low warm sun raking across ruts with real soft shadows, grass clumps growing in the road's crown, and a natural depth-of-field falloff to the houses.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The ruts are smooth rounded grooves, like sculpted sand, with little packed-mud grit, stones or debris. The water in the centre rut is a pale blurry strip with no clear reflection. The grass clumps are similar in size and evenly spaced.

pictures.strongest_point: The thatch and timber houses in the background have some texture.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The ground is an extreme stretched, crinkled noise texture. The water channels are flat grey ribbons. Weed sprites are sparse and identical. The trees are low-poly. The background is flat green and the light flat. Nothing reads as soil.

pictures.strongest_point: The puddle in the rut has a crisp, believable sky reflection. The tall grass verge on the right is convincing.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The road looks like pale beach sand or plaster, smooth and washed out. Pebbles are stamped evenly across it like dots. The ruts are soft sculpted grooves. There are no leaves, straw, dung or mud colour shifts. The light is flat and greyish.

pictures.strongest_point: Strong dappled sunlight with real cast shadows, wet ruts with reflections, and lively detail density.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The stones are all similar round green-grey pebbles, like candy, scattered evenly. Flat orange leaf slivers look like paper cut-outs. The grass blades are wide and bright, game-like. The ground between the stones is smooth and blurry. The colour is oversaturated.

best_per_view.why: It has the richest, most natural aerial look: warm raking sun, a dense, varied forest, and varied field and path surfaces. D is close but has a pine cutting through a hut, a concrete-like road and empty uniform lawns. B has cloned lollipop trees, and C is low-poly.

Golden light, a real reflective puddle, grass growing in the road and atmospheric depth make it the only one that nearly passes as a photo. A's water looks painted blue, D's foliage and cottage are stylised, and B is low-poly.

Weathered grey timber, a mossy roof, real-looking spruces, warm low light and natural grass. Its only big faults are black puddles and new-looking posts. C has dotted pebbles and black blotches, A is clean and toy-like, and D is low-poly.

The meadow, sky, treeline and hazy distant cottage are all photographic. The main fault is a roof that reads as scales rather than thatch. B has floating straws and streaky thatch, C has a fabric-like thatch and confetti flowers, and A is low-poly.

Raking warm light, convincing soft shadows in the ruts and grass rooted in the road's crown read most like a real photo. C is washed out with stamped pebbles, D has candy-like stones and paper leaves, and B is a stretched noise texture.

results.overall_note:
The four sets of pictures differ a great deal. In every view one picture is plainly not a photograph: low-poly faceted trees, cartoon hills, a flat sky and stretched ground textures. Those score 1.5 to 2. The best pictures in each view (1A, 2C, 3B, 4D, 5A) come closest to passing as photos. Low warm sun, dense believable grass and real spruce forests carry them. They still fall short of photographic, mainly through surfaces that are too clean and too regular: spotless plaster and new timber, thatch that reads as felt, fabric or scales, haystacks as perfect domes, and roads that look like smooth sculpted sand. The faults that give the computer away most often, across all makers, are:
- pebbles scattered evenly like a stamped pattern
- puddles drawn as black holes or painted blue streaks
- stylised comb-like conifer foliage
- straws floating in the air (4B)
- a tree passing through a building (1D)
- flowers sprinkled like confetti
- grass made of identical tufts on a flat base
No picture scores above 7.5. Weathering, dirt where the walls meet the ground, irregular thatch, and uneven debris on the ground would do the most to close the gap to a real photograph.

pictures.strongest_point: Reads as a real village cut out of a dense mixed forest: thatched half-timbered cottages, round thatched huts, haystacks, fenced strip fields and branching two-track cart roads all sit in the clearing.
pictures.most_visible_faults: From above the roads are thin, even-width ribbons with tidy edges and no visible mud, puddles or weeds. The clearing is a uniform mown lawn, which reads as kept, not unkept. No building clearly reads as the stable.

pictures.strongest_point: The forest ring is convincing, and the rutted dirt roads branch to each cottage the way cart tracks would.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Game-asset look: lollipop trees, flat pale green grass with even spots, a bare brown band under the forest edge. The cottages are plain grey boxes with little mediaeval character, and almost no props can be seen. The roads are flat beige strips with faint lines, not mud.

pictures.strongest_point: The mediaeval cues are clear: thatched half-timbered longhouse and red-framed cottage, a stone cottage, a well, barrels, sacks and a haystack.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Not in a forest: it is an open field with one row of low-poly trees standing on bare sand, in front of a painted mountain backdrop. The road is a flat reddish band with only faint ruts. Lighting and materials are flat and toy-like.

pictures.strongest_point: A strong forest clearing setting with crossing two-track cart roads, thatched cottages, haystacks and fences.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The roads are wide, pale and perfectly even, with crisp edges and twin lines like tram rails. They look graded and tidy, not unkept. Large areas of empty mown grass, fewer cottages and props than needed, and lone white birches stand oddly in the open.

pictures.strongest_point: A rutted track with a line of hoof or foot prints down the middle and stones, past a thatched half-timbered cottage, a well and a small open shed, with the forest closing in behind.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The puddle is a flat cyan sheet with sharp edges that looks pasted on. The road is smooth grey sand like a beach, with shallow ruts and few weeds, and the edge between grass and road is abrupt.

pictures.strongest_point: Deep twin ruts holding water, and a clearly mediaeval cast: thatched longhouse with barrels, stone cottage, red half-timbered house, haystack.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The road surface is a coarse bark-like texture heaped into ridges like a ploughed bed, and the ruts read as irrigation ditches. Weeds are sparse sticks on flat pale ground. Low-poly trees stand in one row in front of hills, so it does not feel like a forest.

pictures.strongest_point: The best cart track of all: two muddy wheel ruts with standing puddles, a weedy centre strip, tall grass verges and a rail fence, leading past thatched half-timbered cottages and a round hut into a dark conifer forest.
pictures.most_visible_faults: No hoof prints are visible. The dirt between the ruts is a fairly uniform sandy tone, and the puddle reflects a very bright, clean sky that looks slightly cut out.

pictures.strongest_point: A convincingly unkept winding road: wet ruts, puddles, twigs, pebbles and a grassy centre strip, running into a hazy wooded valley.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The fir tree on the right has striped, comb-like fronds that look broken. The cottages are clean white plaster with smooth grey roofs and look like modern holiday cottages rather than mediaeval ones. There are no hoof prints.

pictures.strongest_point: A plausible timber stable with an open front, stall partitions and a hay-hoist beam with rope, plus a cart resting on its shafts, barrels and a trough, with forest behind.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The yard is a flat, clean, pale dirt plane with no hoof prints, ruts, dung or mud. The foreground grass is evenly spaced clumps on a flat green carpet, and the building is too neat and uniform.

pictures.strongest_point: A believable stable in a conifer forest: open stall fronts with half-doors, a mossy shingle roof, water trough, hitching rail, bucket, tipped cart, paddock fence, and a trampled muddy yard with a wheel arc.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The puddles read as dark brown stains or holes rather than water. The stall interior is too dark to show that it is empty. The planking is clean, even grey.

pictures.strongest_point: The empty stable reads best here: stall partitions and a hay rack are visible inside, half-doors stand open, and a hitching rail, bucket, cart, haystack and fence surround a yard with curving wheel ruts, all against dense firs.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The foreground puddle is a black blob that looks like a hole. Grey-green pebbles are sprinkled evenly like confetti across the yard, and the ground has no hoof prints.

pictures.strongest_point: A dark wattle-walled shed on a stone footing with an open door and mossy shingles, which has some rustic character.
pictures.most_visible_faults: It reads as a generic shed, not a stable: no trough, rail or hay. The foreground ground is a noisy reddish bark-like texture with grey blotches, not mud. Low-poly trees, including an umbrella-shaped one, stand on flat sand in front of a painted hill backdrop, so there is no forest.

pictures.strongest_point: The stone well with windlass, rope and bucket is a strong mediaeval prop, alongside barrels and sacks by a thatched half-timbered cottage.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Faceted low-poly trees in a row and a flat green backdrop instead of a forest. The infill walls look like flagstone, not wattle and daub, and the thatch is a smeared flat texture. Weeds are thin sticks on flat grass, and the rutted road at the left is a noisy texture strip.

pictures.strongest_point: A solidly mediaeval cottage: timber frame with braces, a barred window, board shutters and door, a stone footing and chimney, a bench, barrel, clay pot and wattle fence in long grass by the forest.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The thatch is a streaky, motion-blurred texture with sparkling stray hairs. The gable is horizontal clapboard, which looks modern, and the white walls are too clean. There is little sense of a lived-in yard.

pictures.strongest_point: The most convincing thatch: thick and fibrous with rounded eaves. It is joined by a chimney pot, shutters, a log pile, barrel, stump, bench, stone steps and wildflowers, with forest and another outbuilding behind.
pictures.most_visible_faults: It looks a bit like a storybook holiday cottage: tidy plaster, a neat split-rail fence and a manicured meadow. The thatch is slightly soft and blurry, and the ground around it is clean.

pictures.strongest_point: A good village context: a timber-framed cottage with barrel, bench and pot, a worn patch at the door, a well and a second cottage beyond, all in long grass ringed by firs and broadleaves.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The roof reads as overlapping scales or tiles, not thatch. The walls are clean and the scene is sparse, with few props and no visible road.

pictures.strongest_point: Reads as heavily used and neglected: deep, branching wheel ruts with a wet sheen, a weedy centre strip, tufts along the edges, soft churned dirt, and fence, log piles and cottages beyond.
pictures.most_visible_faults: No clear hoof prints. The dirt is a fairly uniform smooth brown like damp sand, and the water in the rut is only a faint sheen rather than a real puddle.

pictures.strongest_point: Twin ruts with water are present, and thatched half-timbered cottages frame the road.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The surface is a crumpled bark or paper texture, not dirt. The water in the ruts is flat grey strips, and the ruts are hard-edged ditches. Weeds are isolated sticks, and low-poly trees and a backdrop wall stand in for the forest.

pictures.strongest_point: The only close-up with clear hoof prints (paired dents at lower left), together with wheel ruts, a rut puddle reflecting sky, pebbles and weeds along the verge.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The ground is pale, dry, beach-like sand rather than mud. The pebbles are sprinkled with even spacing, and the puddle is a crisp, too-clean blue cut-out.

pictures.strongest_point: The richest unkept detail: muddy ruts with water, a lush weed hump in the centre, fallen leaves, twigs and churned mud, with fence and stone cottages beyond.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The pebbles are near-identical round greenish beads scattered everywhere. The water in the right rut is a streaky frosted sheet rather than a reflective puddle, the leaves look like flat paper chips, and there are no hoof prints.

best_per_view.why: It has the most complete request on show: a clearing deep in mixed forest, branching rutted cart roads, the most cottages, round huts, haystacks, fences and fields. D has the same setting but fewer buildings and wide, tidy, rail-like roads. B is game-like, and C is not in a forest at all.

It is the clearest horse-and-cart track: muddy twin ruts with puddles, a weedy centre strip and tall verges, running between thatched half-timbered cottages into a dark forest. A's puddle looks pasted on, D's cottages look modern and its fir is broken, and B's road reads as a ploughed bed.

It best shows the stable is empty: partitions and a hay rack are visible inside the open stalls, with a hitching rail, bucket, cart, haystack and a yard marked by wheel ruts, against a fir forest. B is close but its stalls are too dark to read. A's yard is too clean, and D is a shed on sand.

It has the only truly convincing thick straw thatch, and a lived-in mediaeval set of props (log pile, stump, barrel, bench, chimney pot) with forest around. B's thatch is smeared, and D's roof reads as scales. A is low-poly with no forest.

Deep branching wheel ruts, a weedy centre strip and natural edge tufts make it read most like a neglected road worn by carts, without game-like pebble scatter. D has more detail but bead-like stones and a fake water sheet. C has hoof prints but looks like dry beach sand, and B is a bark texture.

results.overall_note: The pictures split sharply into two groups. The realistic, forest-ringed builds deliver the request reasonably well (scores 6 to 8). The low-poly build fails the forest test in every view: tree rows in front of a painted hill backdrop on bare sand. It also fails the road test, with bark-like ridged textures and flat grey water strips, so it sits at 3 to 4.5 despite good mediaeval props (well, barrels, sacks). Faults shared by the realistic builds: puddles are rarely right (flat cyan sheets, black holes, or frosted streaks), and pebbles are sprinkled with even spacing. Hoof prints appear in only two pictures. Stable yards and village lawns are too clean and mown for "unkept", and from above the roads read as tidy graded paths with twin lines rather than churned mud. The cottages are clearly mediaeval in timber frame and thatch, but walls are uniformly clean, and some roofs read as scales or smeared texture rather than straw. The strongest single pictures are the eye-level cart track with puddles and centre weeds (view 2 C) and the rut close-up with branching wet ruts (view 5 A). The most convincing empty stable is view 3 C.

pictures.strongest_point: Warm, low raking sun with long shadows and soft haze gives real mood and depth. The mixed spruce and broadleaf forest ring, the strip fields and garden plots at right, hay domes, fences and footpaths to doors make it read as a farmed, working clearing.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Everything is too tidy: an evenly mown, single-colour lawn, a perfectly round forest edge, and roofs and walls with no grime. The wheel ruts read as two thin parallel lines, like tram rails. There is no sign of life (no smoke, carts, woodpiles, washing or animals). The bottom cottage is half-buried in trees and the top-right house is hidden behind a tree.

pictures.strongest_point: An open, readable layout with a winding track, cottages spaced around it and some autumn colour in the canopy. The shadows show a clear sun direction.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Bright lime grass with a speckled, sprinkled texture looks like a game terrain. The lollipop trees stand alone like props. A bare brown soil band runs right round the forest edge, which looks unnatural. The track is thin and pasted-on, the houses are small, dark and lack detail, and a cottage is cut by the left frame edge. The light is flat and midday, with little mood.

pictures.strongest_point: The buildings themselves have some character: half-timbering, thatch, a well, barrels and a haystack.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Faceted low-poly trees, a painted backdrop of cartoon hills with snow caps, and an empty gradient sky. There is a hard line between the grass and a sandy plain, and no actual forest around the village, just one row of trees. The ground texture is flat and tiled, the light is grey with no mood, and a haystack is cut off at the bottom edge. Unusable as a documentary backdrop.

pictures.strongest_point: Dense, believable spruce and broadleaf forest around a large clearing, with a clear road junction and wheel ruts. The conifers in the foreground frame the shot and give depth.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The ruts look like railway tracks. The light is cooler and flatter than it should be, and the right half is a big empty lawn. Isolated white birches in the clearing look like placed props. Few buildings show, so the village feels empty. The bottom cottage is blocked by a spruce, and the grass and roofs are uniform and unweathered.

pictures.strongest_point: A convincing tall, mixed grass verge and a plausible thatched half-timbered cottage. The road leads the eye to a dark spruce and birch treeline under a soft sky, and footprints are pressed into the track.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The puddle is a flat, uniform blue strip that reads like a painted decal or plastic sheet. The road is a smooth, pale sand bed with a raised, knife-edged berm against the grass. The cottage walls are spotless with no splash or grime at the base. The cottage is cut off at the left edge and the composition is static and centred.

pictures.strongest_point: Lived-in props by the houses (barrels, sacks, a haystack, a cart) and a clear one-point view down the street.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The 'road' is two raised, ploughed-looking ridges with flat water channels, more like a field drill than a cart track. Weed sprites float on bare, flat ground. The trees are faceted low-poly against a flat green wall of hills. The lighting is shadowless and flat, the sky is an empty gradient, and the bark-like road texture is stretched and tiled.

pictures.strongest_point: The best street composition. The rail fence in the foreground leads into the cottage on the left third, and the track recedes past further cottages and a round hut. Grass grows down the crown of the track, a rut puddle reflects the sky, and low warm sun catches the fence and seed heads.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The two distant cottages are identical copies. All the walls are clean, with no mud splash, wear or repairs. The puddle is a bit too mirror-bright and sharp-edged. The round hut looks odd and unexplained, the far end of the street is empty of people or animals, and the cottage is in flat shade.

pictures.strongest_point: Strong depth and atmosphere: morning haze and aerial perspective, a track winding uphill past several houses, puddles in the ruts, and wildflowers and fences along the verges.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The big spruce on the right is rendered as combed, striped feather shapes and looks broken. The thatch is a smooth clay shell with no straw texture, and the plaster walls are spotless. The bottom-left ground has a tiled cobble-like pattern, and the sky is washed-out and blank. The overall look is stylised game art rather than documentary-real.

pictures.strongest_point: Good set dressing for a working stable: an open-bay barn with a shingle roof, a hay-hoist rope, a lantern, a two-wheeled cart, barrels and a water trough, in a sensible three-quarter view.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The foreground grass is stiff clumps of blades stuck on a flat, bright green ground, which reads as a game engine. The barn wood is uniform new tan with no weathering, rot or dirt, and the roof shingles are too regular. The light is hazy and washed out, and the tree at left has a combed, fern-like texture. The yard is smooth and featureless.

pictures.strongest_point: The most believable stable: silver-grey weathered boards, a mossy shingle roof, and a trodden mud yard with puddles. It has a trough, bucket, hitching rail and cart, natural tall grass in the foreground, a dark spruce wall behind, and warm side light.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The puddles are flat black patches that read as holes or oil. The boards are evenly grey with no dirt splash, dung or straw at the base. The interior is just darkness with no stalls or tack visible. The spruces behind are repeated clones, and the mud yard is smooth and uniform.

pictures.strongest_point: An open front shows the stalls inside, and there are mossy roof shingles, a hitching rail, a bucket, a cart and a haystack behind the fence. It reads clearly as a stable.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Head-on and flat, with half the frame given to bland ground. A black puddle in the foreground reads as a hole in the floor. The pebbles are scattered like even polka dots, a dark shadow blob floats under the hitching rail, and the moss patches are evenly sprinkled, like decals. The building sits in dull shade and the cart is cut off at the right edge.

pictures.strongest_point: The roof has some colour variation and moss, and the stone plinth and plank doors give it a basic farm-building read.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Huge faceted low-poly tree crowns and a cartoon spruce stand in front of a flat painted hill backdrop. The foreground is a noisy, tiled bark-like texture that looks like mulch at the wrong scale. There are no shadows and the light is dead, the stone plinth has cartoon outlines, and there are almost no props. Not usable.

pictures.strongest_point: The stone well and bucket in the foreground are nicely textured and give the frame a foreground layer. Sacks and barrels by the door hint at life.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Faceted low-poly trees fill the top half and stand on bare sand in front of a flat green wall. The plaster has cartoon crack lines, and the thatch is a flat, shiny yellow slab. The ground is flat with floating weed sprites, the track at left is a stretched bark texture, and the lighting is shadowless.

pictures.strongest_point: Close, tactile detail: smudged plaster panels with hairline cracks, a stone plinth, shutters, a bench, a barrel and a clay pot. Natural tall grass in the foreground and good daylight.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Loose straw hairs float in a halo over the thatch like fur, and the thatch itself looks brushed and blurry. The ridge is cut off by the top of the frame, so the house is crammed in. The timber is clean and even, with no rot or green at the base, and there is no context for the village beyond the house.

pictures.strongest_point: The most lived-in dressing: a rail fence framing the foreground, a woodpile, a chopping stump, stone steps, a bench, a barrel and a chimney pot. Soft hazy light and a barn fading into the distance give mood and depth.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The thatch reads as a brushed carpet or fabric, too smooth and puffy. The window frames are chunky and stylised, and the openings look shallow. The wildflowers are sprinkled evenly like confetti. The tree at right is made of flat paper-like leaf cards, and the walls lack dirt, so the whole look leans illustrative.

pictures.strongest_point: The best cottage frame: the whole house shown three-quarter, with a neighbouring cottage and well behind for depth, a mixed spruce and broadleaf backdrop, a real cloudy sky and believable rough meadow grass in the foreground.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The thatch pattern reads as overlapping scales or shingles rather than straw. The walls are clean, with no splash line, wear or repairs. It is sparsely dressed, with one barrel, a pot and a bench. The gable side is flat and grey, the light is a bit low-contrast, and there is a dark muddy patch in the grass with no reason to be there.

pictures.strongest_point: Warm, low sun rakes across several braided wheel ruts, a wet streak runs in the main rut, and grass grows on the crown and verges exactly where it would. A fence and cottages in the background anchor it in the village.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The soil reads as soft, blurry beach sand rather than compacted earth, with a low-resolution, smeared surface. The rut walls are too evenly smooth. There is almost no debris (no stones, twigs, leaves, dung or hoof prints), and the background buildings are cut off at the top edge.

pictures.strongest_point: Low eye-level framing with village houses at the end of the track gives a clear sense of place.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The ground is a stretched, smeared bark-like texture with visible tiling. The water in the ruts is flat grey strips that look like metal rails. Single weed sprites are dotted evenly, and the trees are faceted low-poly in front of a flat green backdrop. The lighting is shadowless and the result is obviously game-like.

pictures.strongest_point: A crisp sky-reflecting puddle in the rut, footprints, a tyre-track crossing and tall dry grass at the verge make a readable track.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The road is pale, grey, powdery sand that looks like a beach or cement dust. The pebbles are spread like even polka dots, and the puddle edge is cut-out sharp and too blue. The berm is a hard, raised edge against the grass. The light is cool and flat with little mood, and the track has no crown grass or debris.

pictures.strongest_point: Rich close detail and warm light: water in both ruts, a grassy crown strip, fallen leaves, twigs, stones half-buried in mud, and wildflowers at the verge. Background houses and a fence give depth.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The pebbles are near-identical smooth round beads scattered too densely and evenly, like sweets. The water is a glossy smear rather than standing water with a waterline. The dirt has a soft, painterly, slightly stylised look, and the leaves are flat cut-outs. Overall it is a touch too staged and clean.

best_per_view.why: Its warm raking light, haze and long shadows give the only real mood. The fields, hay domes, fences and footpaths make it read as a working, farmed clearing. D has similar assets but colder light, an emptier lawn and prop-like birches. B looks like game terrain and C is low-poly with a painted backdrop.

It has the best layered composition: a foreground fence, the cottage on the left third, and a track that recedes past more houses. Grass grows down the middle of the track and a rut puddle reflects the sky, all in warm, low light. A's puddle is a blue decal and its framing is static, D is stylised with a broken spruce, and B is low-poly.

It is the only stable that looks aged and used: weathered grey boards, a mossy roof, a churned mud yard, a trough and cart, real grass and warm light against dark spruce. C has the same assets but is shot flat and frontal with a black-hole puddle. A is new, clean wood on game grass, and D is low-poly.

It shows the whole house in context, with a neighbouring cottage and well behind and convincing meadow grass and sky, so it is closest to a real location. C has richer props but a carpet-like thatch and an illustrative look. B crops the ridge and has floating straw hairs, and A is low-poly.

Warm low light with braided ruts, wet streaks and grass growing on the crown and verges is the most natural and atmospheric. D has more debris but candy-like pebbles and a stylised dirt surface, C is pale beach sand with polka-dot stones, and B is a smeared low-poly texture.

results.overall_note: The four sets split clearly. One recurring look is low-poly: faceted trees, painted hill backdrops, flat shadowless light and stretched bark-like ground textures. It scores 2 to 3 in every view and is not usable for a documentary. The other three are photoreal or semi-photoreal and land between 5 and 7.5. None of them is ready to shoot without set dressing, because they share the same faults. Everything is too clean: walls have no splash line, rot, moss at the base or repairs, and the yards have no dung, straw, tools, washing, smoke or people-traces. Scatter is uniform, with pebbles like polka dots or sweets, flowers like confetti and cloned spruces. Water is the weakest element and shows up as black holes, blue decals or glossy smears instead of standing puddles with waterlines. Thatch reads as fur, carpet, clay or scales rather than straw. The best frames (2C, 1A, 3B, 4D, 5A) win on warm raking light, layered foregrounds and grass growing where traffic would not crush it. Before using any of them I would vary the scatter, add mud and weathering at the base of every building, add working clutter and smoke, fix the puddles, and break up the cloned trees and houses.
